newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle astronauts to return one day early.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle astronauts to return one day early.

text.p: Astronauts aboard the shuttle Columbia will return to earth on Thursday morning, 24 hours earlier than expected, to avoid bad weather forecast for landing sites in Florida and on the U.S. West Coast, NASA said on Wednesday.

"If the weather looks good, then we will go ahead and land tomorrow," flight director Wayne Hale told reporters. If all goes as planned, the shuttle would land at 7:33 a.m. EST (1233 GMT) on Thursday at Kennedy Space Centre, he said.

The decision to call the shuttle home early came after one of the orbiter's three navigation units failed early on Wednesday, and after a stuck airlock hatch forced NASA to cancel a pair of planned spacewalks.

Hale said the weather was "the primary factor" although the failure of the navigation equipment and the hatch problem "played a small role" in moving up the landing date. The two malfunctions "certainly indicate that you ought to button things up and be prepared to come down at the earliest opportunity," he said.
"We would like to land the shuttle tomorrow in Florida," Hale said. "If the weather dictates otherwise, we have options at Edwards Air Force Base (in California) or we can stay up several more days."
NASA managers said weather forecasts called for rainy, unstable weather in central Florida on Friday, and poor weather at a backup landing site in California.
